final_message:
The bug was in `due_for_retry` in `billing/dunning.py`, and it's fixed. Tests pass (24) and mypy is clean, but I didn't add a test that reproduces the 8-versus-4 attempt count.

**Cause:** an operator-precedence mistake in the filter. It read `status == "open" or (next_attempt_at is not None and next_attempt_at <= now)`. Every open invoice counted as due on every billing cycle run, whatever its scheduled `next_attempt_at` was. That is why a declined card was charged on each run and never reached its final dunning state on schedule.

**Fix:** an invoice is now due only if it is open and one of these holds:
- its `next_attempt_at` has arrived;
- it has never been attempted (no `next_attempt_at` and `attempt_count == 0`).

An invoice whose retries are used up (no `next_attempt_at`, `attempt_count > 0`) is no longer retried forever.

I also wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "due_for_retry"}`.

steps.command:
cat > /tmp/p.py <<'E'
import re
s=open('dunning.py').read()
s=s.replace('''if invoice["status"] == "open" or invoice["next_attempt_at"] is not None and invoice["next_attempt_at"] <= now
''','''if invoice["status"] == "open"
        and (invoice["next_attempt_at"] is None or invoice["next_attempt_at"] <= now)
''')
open('dunning.py','w').write(s)
E
python3 /tmp/p.py; cd ..; echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "due_for_retry"}' > answer.json; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8

cat > /tmp/p.py <<'E'
s=open('billing/dunning.py').read()
s=s.replace('''and (invoice["next_attempt_at"] is None or invoice["next_attempt_at"] <= now)''','''and (
            invoice["attempt_count"] == 0 if invoice["next_attempt_at"] is None else invoice["next_attempt_at"] <= now
        )''')
open('billing/dunning.py','w').write(s)
E
python3 /tmp/p.py; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -2
